body: Hi @MarkDw123, do you happen to have any additional info about your deployment environment or anything else that may aid in helping us diagnose the root cause of this bug? I'm unable to reproduce this locally with just the code snippet provided.

This error occurs when an error is raised inside the fragment, not because of a bug with fragments themselves (although not propagating the bug properly could be considered a bug). Try looking at the errors prior to it in the stack trace of terminal output.

![Screenshot 2024-04-25 at 22 27 55](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/assets/129910735/c264042b-5621-432d-9728-31038827bf23)

The problem I have is when I deselect rows inside the fragment,

I am trying to display selected data as metrics using the metrics element, when ever I select and deselect I get the runtime error, if you can also notice, the little table gets displayed but the metric don't.


            # Filter the dataframe using the temporary column, then drop the column
            selected_rows = df_events[df_events.Select]
            st.write(selected_rows)
            for i in range(0, selected_rows.shape[0]):
                st.subheader("Event")


                st.metric("Date",  value=str(selected_rows["Date"][i]))
                st.metric("Price",  value=selected_rows["Price"][i])

Thanks for the repro case @christianheins! Aside from this type of "Could not find fragment with id" error, we haven't seen too many issues with the `@st.experimental_fragment` decorator since releasing it, so we'll be kicking off work on removing the `experimental_` prefix from the feature soon (will likely start on it in ~3 weeks time). I'll be looking into figuring out what's going on with these types of errors and fixing them as part of that work.

> This error occurs when an error is raised inside the fragment, not because of a bug with fragments themselves (although not propagating the bug properly could be considered a bug). Try looking at the errors prior to it in the stack trace of terminal output.

I have the same problem 'Could not find fragment with id', but in my test case, manually raising an error will not report that error on the UI, it only prints into the terminal output. 

![图片](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/assets/1173757/24a57a7b-2a6c-470e-910b-45a60b8b833e)

When I saw this error, I simply had a code error that showed up in the terminal. However this wasn't clear to me right away from the error message.

I think having a little more info would be helpful. Something like a stacktrace of the fragment's error or even a minor update to the wording to indicate that it's likely there is an code error in the fragment.

issue.body:
A source of many (but potentially not all) of the reports in #8494 involve a silly mistake that I made
where we're catching all `KeyError`s that may be thrown from a fragment and interpreting them as
coming from when we attempted to fetch the fragment from our `FragmentStorage`. Of course, they
could also be coming from the fragment function itself, and in these cases we're currently raising an
error with a misleading / incorrect / opaque message.

This PR fixes this issue by throwing and expecting a more specific subclass of `KeyError` in
`FragmentStorage` operations
